THE McGILL DAILY, TWO KANAWANA RECRUITMENT ADVERTISEMENTS
20 May 1948 and 25 May 1949 — the camp buying space in a university newspaper

Identifiers: McGillLibrary-mcgill-daily-v37-n100-may-20-1948-5382
             McGillLibrary-mcgill-daily-v38-n100-may-25-1949-5479
Found 2026-09-07 by the whole-corpus sweep of 9,890 McGill student publication
items under p_479. "Kanawana" occurs exactly once in each issue, in the
advertisement. Both fall in the last week of May, at the end of term.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
20 MAY 1948
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  "FIVE VACANCIES on our Counsellor Staff
   Phone: R. D. Locke, Director
   Y.M.C.A. Kamp Kanawana.  MA. 8331
   for an interesting, healthful and profitable summer."

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
25 MAY 1949
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  "FOUR VACANCIES on our Counsellor Staff
   Phone: R. D. Locke, Director
   Y.M.C.A. Kamp Kanawana.  MA. 8331
   For an interesting, healthful and profitable summer
   CAMP SITUATED IN LAURENTIANS — 3 LAKES — 600 ACRES OF WOODED PROPERTY"

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WHAT THEY GIVE, CHECKED AGAINST THE DESTINATION FIRST
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. TWO DATED ATTESTATIONS OF R. D. LOCKE AS "DIRECTOR", IN PUBLIC, UNDER HIS
   OWN NAME AND TELEPHONE NUMBER. wiki/people/roy-locke.md has him becoming
   "Camp Chief of Kamp Kanawana in the summer of 1947" and holding the Montreal
   YMCA's Boys' Work and Camping portfolio to September 1954, on internal
   association evidence. These are two outside, dated documents from inside that
   span. The TITLE is the small thing worth noting: the association's own
   records call him Camp Chief; the advertisement he placed calls him DIRECTOR.
   Which is what a camp would put in a newspaper, and a caution against reading
   title variation in this period as evidence of a change in post.

2. THE CAMP RECRUITED COUNSELLORS OUT OF THE UNIVERSITIES, AND THIS IS THE
   EARLIEST DIRECT EVIDENCE OF IT HELD HERE. The pattern this project has been
   building all day from the other side -- Sir George Fellowship men staffing
   the camps, the 1962 Georgian advertisement for Kanawana staff, the 1993
   Daily piece about a collective who "know each other from Camp Kanawana" --
   has its plainest instance here: the camp buying display space in a student
   newspaper in the last week of term, twice, in consecutive years.

3. FIVE VACANCIES IN 1948 AND FOUR IN 1949, both advertised in late May. That
   is a late-season gap of a known size in each year, which is a different kind
   of number from a staff total: it says what the camp still needed after its
   own channels had been worked.

4. "3 LAKES — 600 ACRES OF WOODED PROPERTY", MAY 1949. This corroborates from
   OUTSIDE the annual reports a figure the wiki holds only from inside them.
   wiki/site/the-kanawana-site.md gives "600 acres" on the authority of "YMCA
   annual reports, 1949-1959" and quotes the 1958 report's "three lakes and a
   part of a fourth, covering some 600 acres". This advertisement is from MAY
   1949 -- the first year of that range -- and states the same two figures in
   public, to strangers, where an overstatement would have been checkable by
   anyone who took the job. It does not resolve the wiki's open question about
   the jump from 600 acres to 1,000, and it does not touch the 1957 report's
   "sixty acres"; it makes the 600 figure independently attested at the range's
   start. Note also that the ad says three lakes flat, where the 1958 report
   says three and part of a fourth.

NULL RESULTS. "Otoreke" 0 and "Perrot" 0 in both issues. Neither advertisement
names a wage, a season length, an age requirement, or any other member of staff.
